title: The key-provider bound test asserts wall-clock time and fails under CI contention
description:
Measured on 2026-09-29 while promoting WCLI-51, from a real red rather than from inspection.

test/key-provider.test.ts:293, the load and create cases of describe("every store call settles within its bound"), sets a 150 ms bound and then asserts elapsed >= 140 AND elapsed < 400 on the wall clock, read with performance.now(). The upper number is a lint on scheduler jitter rather than on the code behaviour, so contention alone can break it.

THE INSTANCE. Run 36565512667, the pull_request workflow for SHA 61aa8a24, failed with "(fail) every store call settles within its bound > load gives up at the bound [474.43ms]" — 474 ms against the 400 ms ceiling. Nothing about the change under test was involved: it touched the vault state document, the reporting module, the error catalogue and their tests, none of which is on this timing path.

IT IS A FLAKE, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Three independent readings:
1. The SAME SHA 61aa8a24 passed the push workflow (run 36565482468, conclusion success) while failing the pull_request workflow. Identical bytes, two outcomes.
2. A re-run of the failed job on the same SHA, changing nothing, returned success.
3. The mechanism is visible in the timings. Run 36565482468 ran 12:02:12Z to 12:02:54Z (42 s) and run 36565512667 ran 12:02:28Z to 12:04:05Z (97 s) — they overlapped by 26 seconds on the same runner group, and the contended run took more than twice as long. Every earlier SHA pair in this repository ran sequentially, 40 or more seconds apart, and passed. This is the first pair that raced.

WHY THE CAUSE IS NOT ONLY THE TEST. The overlap happens because a push to dev fires both the push and the pull_request workflows for one SHA, and .github/workflows/ci.yml scopes concurrency per ref, so the two do not cancel each other. That is a CI configuration question and it is deliberately left open here: the test should be robust whether or not the configuration is changed.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE FILE. Two blocks below, the test "the default bound is 10 s and is the one applied" asserts the same kind of bound deterministically by replacing globalThis.setTimeout, recording the delay it was given and asserting on that value. The technique this task needs is therefore eight lines away rather than something to invent, and the wall-clock assertion should either go or be widened far enough that no runner can break it.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN JUST RETRIED. A gate that is re-run whenever it is inconvenient is how a real regression eventually gets waved through, and this one will recur on the next overlapping pair.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The store-call bound is asserted deterministically, or its wall-clock ceiling is wide enough that runner contention cannot break it
The assertion still fails when the provider stops honouring its timeout, proven by mutating the check rather than by observing it green

Every other wall-clock upper bound in the suite that runner contention can break is swept and either widened with a measured margin or made deterministic; the starting list is backup.test.ts:538 (under 2000 ms), setup.test.ts:201 (under 5000 ms) and vault-store.test.ts:626 (under 2000 ms), alongside key-provider.test.ts:293 from the first criterion

plan: Make the key-provider load and create bound deterministic with a shared immediate-timer helper, keeping the configured bound and the refusal as the assertions
Prove the assertion reddens by mutating the provider, not by observing it green: a bound taken from the default instead of the configured value, and a bound applied as Infinity
Same treatment for setup.test.ts unresponsive-store case, whose 5 s ceiling equals Bun default test timeout and so could never fire
Sweep every remaining wall-clock upper bound in the suite, measure each survivor idle and under induced CPU load, and record the margin beside the assertion
Run the full check plus a repeat-run stability pass, open the PR, and close the task with the sweep and mutation evidence
implementationNotes:
SCOPE WIDENED, 2026-09-29, on a relay from opum-agent (OPAG-768, cross-session, 12:41:45Z) and verified here in the source rather than taken on the message. The fleet survey found three more wall-clock ceilings in this suite beyond key-provider.test.ts:293:

- test/backup.test.ts around line 538: expect Date.now() - started toBeLessThan(2_000), the FIFO read-never-blocks bound.
- test/setup.test.ts around line 201: expect performance.now() - started toBeLessThan(5_000), the unresponsive-store bound.
- test/vault-store.test.ts around line 626: expect performance.now() - started toBeLessThan(2_000), the vault-busy bound.

All three verified by reading the lines. They differ in shape from the instance this task was filed for: each asserts an upper bound only, with no lower bound, so contention alone can still break them when a starved runner pushes a correct operation past the ceiling, but there is no jitter window to also fall short of. The fix is the same family, which is why they are one task rather than a new one; a third acceptance criterion now names them and asks for the rest of the suite to be swept in the same pass.
